transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me today. I really appreciate it. 

Um, I hope I'm explaining this right, but I'm here because... well, I've been having a little trouble keeping my mind on things at work. I'm a computer support specialist, and I always try really hard to do a good job, but lately, I just can't seem to stay on a task long enough to finish it. Even when it's something really important. 

Like, I'll start tracing a client's network problem, which is something I should be able to do easily, and ten minutes will go by and I'll realize I've just reread the exact same log entries three times... and I still don't know what they actually say. It's a bit embarrassing to admit, honestly, because I really don't want to let my clients down. Does that... does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Have you been finding yourself feeling constantly anxious or worried lately?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say I'm constantly anxious. I mean, I care a lot about my job, and I guess I get a little stressed when I feel like I'm falling behind, but... it's not like a constant worry or panic or anything like that. I'm usually a pretty positive person, actually. I just... I just want to make sure I'm doing things right, you know? Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm not misunderstanding the question.
Did you experience similar difficulties with attention or staying focused when you were growing up in school?

Well, um... I suppose I did, yes. Actually, my mother still jokes about it sometimes. She says my old grade school report cards always mentioned that I was a really bright student—which is nice, you know, because I really did want to do well! 

But... well, the teachers also wrote that I almost never stayed in my seat. And I guess I had a bit of a habit of blurting out answers in class. I think I was just really eager to participate, but I know it probably wasn't the most polite thing to do. Oh, and I'd somehow lose my homework, even when I knew for a fact I had finished it the night before. It's a little embarrassing to think back on, to be honest. I was just an energetic kid who was a bit disorganized, I guess. 

Is that... does that answer your question? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of background history.
